title: Email: SMTP, IMAP, POP3S, SPF, DKIM and DMARC

videos.script: Email is the oldest service most people use every day, and one of the first things they call IT about. A message that never arrived. A message that bounced. A message that looked like it came from the boss, and did not. {{calls}} Behind each of those is a handful of protocols. SMTP carries the message from server to server. IMAP and POP3 let a person read it. And three DNS records, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, let a receiving server decide whether the sender is who they claim to be. {{protocols}} In this lesson you will send a message by typing SMTP yourself, to see how little there is to it. Then you will send one the way a mail program does, with a password and encryption. You will read it with IMAP and POP3, by hand. {{steps}} You will read the headers a message collects on its way. You will watch a forged invoice get turned away by DMARC. And you will read a bounce and a queue, the two places where the reason for a missing message is written down. {{trouble}}
